Simulate data shaped like a KECC quality measure

Source: R/sim_kecc.R
sim_kecc.Rd

Patients nested in providers with repeated observations per patient, a provider effect, a patient random effect and a few covariates. The outcome is binary per row (a patient-month, say), binomial out of a number of trials per row (days at risk, say), continuous, or a survival time with censoring, split into counting-process rows.

Usage

sim_kecc(
  n_providers = 50,
  provider_size = c(15, 60),
  rows_per_patient = c(1, 6),
  type = c("binary", "binomial", "continuous", "survival"),
  trials = c(20, 31),
  n_covariates = 3,
  beta = NULL,
  gamma_sd = 0.5,
  patient_sd = 0.5,
  base_rate = 0.25,
  sigma = 1,
  base_hazard = 0.5,
  follow_up = c(0.5, 2),
  seed = NULL
)

Arguments

n_providers

number of providers.

provider_size

range of the number of patients per provider; sizes are drawn uniformly between the two values.

rows_per_patient

range of the number of rows per patient.

type

"binary" (one trial per row), "binomial" (n trials per row), "continuous" or "survival".

trials

range of the number of trials per row for type = "binomial".

n_covariates

number of covariates (at least 1): x1 is a patient-level standard normal, x2 a patient-level 0/1 with probability 0.4, and any further covariates are row-level standard normals (patient-level for a survival outcome).

beta

covariate coefficients; by default 0.5, -0.4, 0.3 recycled.

gamma_sd

standard deviation of the provider effects around the logit of base_rate (binary, binomial) or around 0 (continuous).

patient_sd

standard deviation of the patient random effect.

base_rate

event probability of an average patient at the median provider (binary and binomial outcomes).

sigma

residual standard deviation of a continuous outcome.

base_hazard, follow_up

for type = "survival": the hazard of an average patient at the median provider (exponential event times), and the range of the censoring time, drawn uniformly. Each patient's follow-up is cut into rows_per_patient consecutive rows (start, stop], the last carrying the event if it came before censoring.

seed

optional random seed.

Value

A data frame with columns provider, patient, n (trials; 1 for binary and continuous outcomes), y and the covariates, one row per observation, in random order; for a survival outcome the columns start, stop and event replace n and y. The true parameters are kept in attr(, "truth"): gamma (named by provider), beta, patient_effect (named by patient).

Examples

d <- sim_kecc(n_providers = 5, seed = 1)
str(attr(d, "truth"))
#> List of 3
#>  $ gamma         : Named num [1:5] -0.572 -1.658 -0.931 -0.851 -1.03
#>   ..- attr(*, "names")= chr [1:5] "P001" "P002" "P003" "P004" ...
#>  $ beta          : Named num [1:3] 0.5 -0.4 0.3
#>   ..- attr(*, "names")= chr [1:3] "x1" "x2" "x3"
#>  $ patient_effect: Named num [1:171] -0.0594 0.0988 -0.5343 -0.4016 -0.5569 ...
#>   ..- attr(*, "names")= chr [1:171] "P001-001" "P001-002" "P001-003" "P001-004" ...
s <- sim_kecc(n_providers = 5, type = "survival", seed = 1)
head(s)
#>   provider  patient     start       stop event         x1 x2         x3
#> 1     P003 P003-010 0.0000000 0.13188650     1  0.1063206  1 -0.2464703
#> 2     P004 P004-027 0.4887299 0.57594207     1  0.4596217  0  0.7048330
#> 3     P002 P002-025 0.8418941 1.06252226     0  0.2222181  0 -0.7610403
#> 4     P002 P002-012 0.5227791 1.03538921     0  0.4345367  1  0.5756203
#> 5     P004 P004-004 0.0000000 0.04786032     0 -0.1296354  0  0.7159321
#> 6     P005 P005-028 0.6503206 0.79878563     0 -0.8846849  1  1.3609245
